stem: A client receiving chronic dialysis says, "My laboratory results look acceptable, but dialysis has disrupted my work, relationships, sleep, and mood." Which nursing response best reflects comprehensive dialysis care?

options.A: Assess how kidney failure and dialysis are affecting physical functioning, emotional well-being, relationships, daily roles, and treatment burden, and communicate these findings to the interdisciplinary team for an individualized plan of care.
options.B: Focus only on laboratory targets because psychosocial and quality-of-life concerns do not need to be incorporated into the dialysis plan if dialysis adequacy measures are acceptable.
options.C: Use one identical quality-of-life response plan for every dialysis client because individual social roles, emotional needs, and treatment burden do not change care planning.
options.D: Delay psychosocial assessment until the client requests treatment withdrawal because routine dialysis care addresses physical treatment needs only.

rationale: CMS requires an individualized comprehensive plan of care for dialysis clients based on the interdisciplinary assessment and changes in the client's condition. The plan must address psychosocial status, including monitoring and social-work interventions, using a standardized mental and physical assessment tool selected by the social worker at regular intervals or more often when needed. Current National Kidney Foundation guidance also recognizes that dialysis can affect physical health, mood, relationships, independence, daily functioning, and overall quality of life. Therefore, A is correct. B excludes required psychosocial care, C conflicts with individualized care planning, and D delays assessment until severe distress or treatment-withdrawal consideration.
educational_objective: Include physical, emotional, social, role-function, and treatment-burden effects in ongoing dialysis quality-of-life assessment and communicate these findings to the interdisciplinary team for individualized care planning.
source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS); National Kidney Foundation
source_document_title: ESRD Clinic Services — Patient Plan of Care; Depression and Dialysis
source_version_date: CMS ESRD Clinic Services current 2026; NKF Depression and Dialysis last updated 2025-08-13
source_locator: CMS 'ESRD Clinic Services' → Patient POC: the interdisciplinary team must develop an individualized comprehensive plan based on assessment and changes in condition. POC Development → Psychosocial status: necessary monitoring and social-work interventions, including counseling/referrals, measured by a standardized mental and physical assessment tool chosen by the social worker at regular intervals or as needed; rehabilitation status should support the level of productive activity desired by the patient. NKF 'Depression and Dialysis' → dialysis-related depression can affect physical health, relationships, daily functioning, treatment adherence, independence, and quality of life.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports individualized psychosocial and mental/physical quality-of-life assessment as part of the dialysis plan of care rather than limiting care to laboratory or physical-treatment measures.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity → Coping/Support Systems/Therapeutic Communication: assess psychosocial adaptation to chronic illness and treatment, identify effects on relationships and roles, and coordinate appropriate psychosocial support.
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — multidimensional quality-of-life assessment in chronic dialysis
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source's broad quality-of-life list into an applied psychosocial assessment and care-planning item using current CMS ESRD requirements. The final item avoids implying that one standardized measure or one fixed response plan applies identically to every client; CMS requires individualized care while allowing the social worker to choose an appropriate standardized mental/physical assessment tool.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Quality of life and psychosocial care planning in chronic dialysis
audit_findings.source_authority: Current CMS ESRD care-plan requirements reinforced by current NKF dialysis mental-health guidance.
audit_findings.currentness: CMS's current 2026 ESRD Clinic Services guidance restates the active 42 CFR Part 494 plan-of-care requirements; NKF updated its dialysis depression resource in 2025.

claim_by_claim.stem: Acceptable laboratory values do not exclude clinically important treatment burden, role disruption, sleep, relationship, or mood concerns.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because CMS requires individualized psychosocial assessment/care planning and NKF recognizes multidimensional effects of dialysis on quality of life.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because psychosocial status is a required care-plan domain and cannot be replaced by laboratory targets alone.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because CMS requires an individualized comprehensive plan based on each client's assessed needs and condition.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because psychosocial assessment and social-work intervention are ongoing components of dialysis care, not services reserved for withdrawal decisions.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Does not claim that a single quality-of-life instrument is mandated nationally; CMS specifically allows a standardized mental/physical tool chosen by the social worker.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to multidimensional psychosocial/quality-of-life assessment and interdisciplinary care planning.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B tests laboratory-only care, C one-size-fits-all planning, and D inappropriate delay of psychosocial assessment. Each is realistic and distinct.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A integrates the client's physical, emotional, social, and role effects into individualized interdisciplinary care.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe how the team should respond to quality-of-life concerns despite acceptable laboratory findings.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity is the strongest fit because the central construct is treatment burden, roles, relationships, coping, and emotional well-being.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited overlap with Q1726. Q1726 tests specific depressive/social-isolation cues and referral; Q1727 tests the broader multidimensional quality-of-life assessment and individualized ESRD care-plan process. The constructs are distinct and no unresolved conflict remains.
